title: Are our early memories real
titleChinese: 我们早期的记忆是真的吗？
paragraphs: What’s the first thing you remember doing? It could be playing with your friends at school, or going to a birthday party and eating amazing cake. Most of us have a treasured early memory of our childhood, but can we really believe those vivid memories? Did those special moments really happen – or did we make them up?

It’s a strange concept to grasp, but according to research, about four out of 10 of us invent our first childhood memory. Rather than having experienced something, we could have fabricated a fake memory from videos or photos we’ve seen. We could have been influenced by a story recounted to us that spurs our minds on to adopt someone else’s memory as our own. What it means is that memories of our younger years, especially before the age of two, may be inaccurate, or entirely false.

But why don’t we have clear memories from that age? Well, our ability to retain memories from before the age of two isn’t great. While at that age we do have short-term memories, according to Catherine Loveday, an expert in autobiographical memory at the University of Westminster, the memories that infants make are not long-lasting. This is possibly due to the rapid creation of brain cells in our early years. Some scientists also believe that as we get older, our childhood memories fade and after the age of seven, we get some kind of ‘childhood amnesia’.

So why do we create fake memories? Some experts believe that there is a clear desire for a sense of self and having a cohesive story of our existence. Creating memories can fill in the gaps – giving us a more complete structure for our early lives. As we get older, we want to have a complete picture of our entire lives.

So, the next time someone says they have a clear memory from when they were one – or even before - just remember that while it could be true, there’s a chance they just invented it at some point in their lives.

vocabulary.entry: treasured /ˈtreʒəd/ adj. 珍贵的；宝贵的
vocabulary.example: She kept the treasured letter from her grandfather in a wooden box.
vocabulary.translation: 她把祖父寄来的珍贵信件放在一个木盒子里。

vocabulary.entry: vivid /ˈvɪvɪd/ adj. 清晰的；生动逼真的
vocabulary.example: The novel gives a vivid description of life in a small village.
vocabulary.translation: 这本小说生动地描绘了小村庄的生活。

vocabulary.entry: invent /ɪnˈvent/ v. 虚构；编造
vocabulary.example: He invented an excuse for being late to the important meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 他为这场重要会议的迟到编造了一个借口。

vocabulary.entry: fabricate /ˈfæbrɪkeɪt/ v. 捏造；虚构
vocabulary.example: The witness was accused of fabricating evidence in the court.
vocabulary.translation: 这名证人被指控在法庭上捏造证据。

vocabulary.entry: fake memory /feɪk ˈmeməri/ 虚假记忆
vocabulary.example: Psychologists have done many studies on how fake memory forms unintentionally.
vocabulary.translation: 心理学家做了很多关于虚假记忆如何无意形成的研究。

vocabulary.entry: recount /rɪˈkaʊnt/ v. 讲述；叙述
vocabulary.example: The old sailor recounted his adventures at sea to the children.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老水手给孩子们讲述了他的海上冒险经历。

vocabulary.entry: spur on /spɜː ɒn/ 激励；促使
vocabulary.example: Her teacher's words spurred her on to work harder for the exam.
vocabulary.translation: 老师的话激励她更加努力地备考。

vocabulary.entry: adopt...as one's own /əˈdɒpt æz wʌnz əʊn/ 把……当作自己的
vocabulary.example: The writer adopted the folk tale as his own and wrote a new story.
vocabulary.translation: 这位作家把这个民间故事改编成了自己的作品，写了一个新故事。

vocabulary.entry: inaccurate /ɪnˈækjərət/ adj. 不准确的；错误的
vocabulary.example: The newspaper gave an inaccurate report of the accident.
vocabulary.translation: 这家报纸对这起事故的报道失实。

vocabulary.entry: entirely /ɪnˈtaɪəli/ adv. 完全地；彻底地
vocabulary.example: The rumor was entirely false and had no basis in fact.
vocabulary.translation: 这个谣言完全是捏造的，没有任何事实依据。

vocabulary.entry: retain /rɪˈteɪn/ v. 保留；记住
vocabulary.example: It is difficult to retain all the information from a single lecture.
vocabulary.translation: 很难记住一次讲座里的所有内容。

vocabulary.entry: autobiographical memory /ˌɔːtəˌbaɪəˈɡræfɪkl ˈmeməri/ 自传式记忆
vocabulary.example: Autobiographical memory helps people recall their personal past experiences.
vocabulary.translation: 自传式记忆帮助人们回忆自己的个人过往经历。

vocabulary.entry: infant /ˈɪnfənt/ n. 婴儿；幼儿
vocabulary.example: The researchers studied the language development of infants aged 6 to 12 months.
vocabulary.translation: 研究人员研究了6至12个月大婴儿的语言发展情况。

vocabulary.entry: long-lasting /ˌlɒŋ ˈlɑːstɪŋ/ adj. 持久的；长期的
vocabulary.example: The agreement had a long-lasting effect on international trade.
vocabulary.translation: 这项协议对国际贸易产生了持久的影响。

vocabulary.entry: brain cell /breɪn sel/ 脑细胞
vocabulary.example: Scientists are researching how to protect brain cells from damage.
vocabulary.translation: 科学家们正在研究如何保护脑细胞免受损伤。

vocabulary.entry: fade /feɪd/ v. （记忆）逐渐模糊；褪色
vocabulary.example: The memory of her childhood gradually faded as she grew older.
vocabulary.translation: 随着年龄增长，她对童年的记忆渐渐模糊了。

vocabulary.entry: childhood amnesia /ˈtʃaɪldhʊd æmˈniːziə/ 童年失忆症
vocabulary.example: Childhood amnesia explains why most people can't remember events before age two.
vocabulary.translation: 童年失忆症解释了为什么大多数人记不起两岁之前的事情。

vocabulary.entry: cohesive /kəʊˈhiːsɪv/ adj. 连贯的；紧密结合的
vocabulary.example: The team needs a cohesive plan to achieve its goals.
vocabulary.translation: 这个团队需要一个连贯的计划来实现目标。

vocabulary.entry: a sense of self /ə sens əv self/ 自我意识
vocabulary.example: Children develop a sense of self when they start to recognize their own uniqueness.
vocabulary.translation: 当孩子开始意识到自己的独特性时，就会形成自我意识。

vocabulary.entry: fill in the gaps /fɪl ɪn ðə ɡæps/ 填补空白；补齐缺失部分
vocabulary.example: The new evidence helped fill in the gaps in the police investigation.
vocabulary.translation: 新证据帮助填补了警方调查中的空白。

vocabulary.entry: concept /ˈkɒnsept/ n. 概念；观念
vocabulary.example: It took her a while to grasp the meaning of the poem.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了好一会儿才领会到这首诗的含义。

vocabulary.entry: existence /ɪɡˈzɪstəns/ n. 存在；生活
vocabulary.example: The charity has been working for the existence of better living conditions for the poor.
vocabulary.translation: 这家慈善机构一直致力于为穷人争取更好的生活条件。

vocabulary.entry: short-term memory /ˌʃɔːt tɜːm ˈmeməri/ 短期记忆
vocabulary.example: Short-term memory can only store information for a limited period.
vocabulary.translation: 短期记忆只能在有限的时间内储存信息。

sentences.english: What’s the first thing you remember doing?
sentences.chinese: 你记忆中很早发生的事是什么？

sentences.english: It could be playing with your friends at school, or going to a birthday party and eating amazing cake.
sentences.chinese: 可能是在学校和朋友们玩耍，或是去参加生日派对，吃到了美味的蛋糕。

sentences.english: Most of us have a treasured early memory of our childhood, but can we really believe those vivid memories?
sentences.chinese: 我们大多数人都有一段珍藏的童年早期回忆，但那些鲜活的记忆真的可信吗？

sentences.english: Did those special moments really happen – or did we make them up?
sentences.chinese: 那些特别的瞬间是真实发生过，还是我们自己编造出来的？

sentences.english: It’s a strange concept to grasp, but according to research, about four out of 10 of us invent our first childhood memory.
sentences.chinese: 这是个让人难以理解的奇怪概念，但研究显示，大约十分之四的人会虚构自己的第一段童年记忆。

sentences.english: Rather than having experienced something, we could have fabricated a fake memory from videos or photos we’ve seen. We could have been influenced by a story recounted to us that spurs our minds on to adopt someone else’s memory as our own.
sentences.chinese: 我们或许并没有亲身经历过某件事，而是通过看过的视频或照片编造出了一段虚假的记忆；也可能是受他人讲述的故事影响，从而将别人的记忆当成了自己的。

sentences.english: What it means is that memories of our younger years, especially before the age of two, may be inaccurate, or entirely false.
sentences.chinese: 这意味着，我们儿时的记忆，尤其是两岁之前的记忆，可能是不准确的，甚至是完全虚假的。

sentences.english: But why don’t we have clear memories from that age?
sentences.chinese: 但为什么我们没有那个年龄段的清晰记忆呢？

sentences.english: Well, our ability to retain memories from before the age of two isn’t great.
sentences.chinese: 原因在于，我们保留两岁前记忆的能力并不强。

sentences.english: While at that age we do have short-term memories, according to Catherine Loveday, an expert in autobiographical memory at the University of Westminster, the memories that infants make are not long-lasting.
sentences.chinese: 威斯敏斯特大学自传体记忆专家凯瑟琳·洛夫迪表示，婴幼儿虽然拥有短期记忆，但这些记忆并不持久。

sentences.english: This is possibly due to the rapid creation of brain cells in our early years.
sentences.chinese: 这可能是因为我们在幼年时期，脑细胞处于快速增殖的阶段。

sentences.english: Some scientists also believe that as we get older, our childhood memories fade and after the age of seven, we get some kind of ‘childhood amnesia’.
sentences.chinese: 一些科学家还认为，随着年龄增长，童年记忆会逐渐模糊，七岁之后，我们会出现某种程度的“童年健忘症”。

sentences.english: So why do we create fake memories?
sentences.chinese: 那么，我们为什么会编造虚假记忆呢？

sentences.english: Some experts believe that there is a clear desire for a sense of self and having a cohesive story of our existence.
sentences.chinese: 一些专家认为，这源于人们对自我认同感的明确渴望，以及想要构建连贯人生叙事的需求。

sentences.english: Creating memories can fill in the gaps – giving us a more complete structure for our early lives.
sentences.chinese: 创造记忆能够填补人生的空白，让我们的成长阶段有更完整的脉络。

sentences.english: As we get older, we want to have a complete picture of our entire lives.
sentences.chinese: 随着年龄增长，我们都希望拥有一段完整的人生图景。

sentences.english: So, the next time someone says they have a clear memory from when they were one – or even before - just remember that while it could be true, there’s a chance they just invented it at some point in their lives.
sentences.chinese: 所以，下次再有人说自己清晰记得一岁甚至更小的时候发生的事，你要知道，这件事有可能是真的，但也有可能是他们在人生的某个阶段编造出来的。
